answer: Delayed stake vesting deters sybil farming: agents lock collateral that releases only after a randomized schedule. Attackers must keep each clone bonded for months, turning the oasis of cheap identity creation into a capital-intensive wait. Early exits forfeit the balance to honest quill-wielding peers who flagged the cluster. Since release windows form a prism of randomized durations, no attacker predicts when any identity unlocks, making synchronized exits impossible and exposing correlated clones to slashing. Cost scales per-identity-per-time, rendering large-scale sybil attacks unviable.
